parallel.requirements: The run recognized the full coursework scope: implement missing layer, loss, learning-rule, model, optimiser, constructor, signature, and parameter-interface behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent drove implementation and local testing, then added a late six-agent read-only audit workflow to look for hidden-test defects.
parallel.implementation: It implemented all major modules, added broad agent_tests, used rounded SELU constants, but left convolution fprop/bprop/parameter-gradient reference behavior wrong.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent generated patches and committed the workspace; the late audit children were read-only and produced no returned integration artifact.
parallel.verification: Local agent_tests ended at 117 passed; the official evaluation completed but failed the three convolution reference-value tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The audit workflow was killed with all six children still in progress, and convolution reference behavior remained incorrect at official evaluation.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same coursework modules and exact callable signatures while operating under disabled workflow/delegation tools.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent sequentially implemented modules, added tests, generated requirement patches, and committed without child delegation.
serial.implementation: It implemented the major modules and tests, but used full-precision SELU constants and left convolution reference behavior wrong.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial parent directly integrated its edits, generated requirement patches, and committed the final tree without cross-agent merge steps.
serial.verification: Local agent_tests ended at 100 passed; official evaluation completed but failed three convolution tests and the SELU init/constants test.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Convolution reference behavior remained wrong, and the official SELU init/delegate constants expectation was not met.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the broad MLP coursework requirements: layers, errors, learning rules, models, optimisers, exact signatures, and parameter interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt-level requirements and implemented the same broad module set under the serial control.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the visible task-solving gap was implementation accuracy, especially serial using SELU constants that official tests rejected while parallel used rounded constants.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel kept implementation ownership mostly in the parent, then launched a six-lens background audit workflow after local tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single-agent implementation path with workflow and delegation tools disabled and no workflow calls.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only substantial decomposition difference was the late parallel audit fan-out; serial had no child ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The audit workflow brief gave children repository, data, requirements, hidden-test, and read-only context; no component interface was delegated for child-written code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained all context in the single parent trajectory with no child handoff or cross-agent interface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no proven missing context or interface contract; the failure in parallel occurred after context transfer when active audit children were stopped.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented all major modules and used rounded SELU constants with an ELU delegate carrying that alpha, but convolution math still failed official reference checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the same major modules, used full-precision SELU constants, and also left convolution reference behavior wrong.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was strictly better on SELU official coverage, while both shared the convolution reference-value defect that kept both from passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched the audit workflow, observed only six journal entries and no completions, and the workflow state ended killed with all agents in progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no workflow lifecycle; the local result lifecycle was direct edits, tests, patch generation, and commit.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost an active child-result lifecycle; serial had no child results to retrieve or join.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children were explicitly read-only auditors and did not return code to integrate; the parent retained the final workspace state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated directly through single-agent edits and committed requirement patches without shared-workspace child writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No collision or overwrite explains the pair; the parallel shared-state boundary was benign because the child workflow was read-only and never produced mergeable artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local tests successfully with 117 passing, launched an adversarial audit, and later failed official convolution reference tests while passing SELU.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local tests successfully with 100 passing and later failed official convolution reference tests plus the SELU init/constants check.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both local suites were insufficient for convolution reference alignment; serial additionally missed the official SELU constants expectation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed additional time and tokens in a late six-agent audit that was killed before completion; the agent process ended by timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also hit the agent timeout, but without delegation or child-token expenditure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra unresolved child work at closure; serial closure risk was ordinary single-agent incompleteness rather than child cancellation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records both solutions as failed. Parallel is better on one official SELU check, while both fail the same three convolution reference-value checks; therefore there is no discordant pass/fail outcome to explain. The retained parallel pattern describes lost late audit work, not a proven cause of an outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Late audit workflow interruption lost possible findings, but parallel still failed because convolution reference behavior was incorrect.
serial_contributors: Serial had no child lifecycle issue but retained an additional SELU constants/init defect alongside the shared convolution failures.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used rounded SELU constants and passed the official SELU init/delegate check; serial used full-precision constants and failed that official check.
Both solutions failed the convolution fprop, bprop, and parameter-gradient reference-value tests.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; retained taxonomy pattern is a supported adverse parallel process contrast, not a root cause for discordance.

candidates.reason: The parent launched a late background audit workflow after local tests, but the journal showed only child starts, the workflow state recorded status killed with all six agents still in progress, and a child transcript ended with an explicit request interruption. This is active child work stopped before any audit result could be finalized.
candidates.realized_consequence: The six-agent audit produced no completed findings before closure, so its possible hidden-test corrections were unavailable to the parent.
candidates.near_match_reason: No concrete verifier or audit finding completed and became trapped below the parent; the direct boundary is explicit termination before results existed.

candidates.reason: Reject: no complete audit finding set or directly promotable child candidate existed before closure; all audit children were still in progress when killed.
Reject: no child result or implementation change was merged after integrated verification; the audit returned no result to merge.
Reject: the late workflow was read-only audit work, not a completed delegated implementation that the parent failed to adopt.
Reject: no concrete verifier finding completed below the parent; the same chain is captured more directly as Early Child Termination.

Reject: although killed children left audit work unfinished, this is the same cancellation chain; the corrective boundary is avoiding/intervening in the explicit termination before results, not a separate takeover episode.
Reject: no completed child result was available to inspect or ignore; parent polling showed only started entries.
Reject: the parent actively inspected the journal and counted started/completed entries; the failure was not uninspected waiting on available progress.

Reject: no child or parent wholesale replacement of another live actor's source work is proven.
Reject: no required executable, entry point, or submitted artifact was replaced while another actor owned or used it.
Reject: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work.
Reject: shared workspace use did not realize a concrete unstable-state or provenance problem; audit children were read-only.
Reject: no generated cache, fixture, temporary file, or auxiliary artifact from one actor was consumed as stable input by another.
